---
title: "RCM2() with several stocks"
output: html_document
---

```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", warning = FALSE, message = FALSE)
library(MSEtool)
library(SAMtool)
```

`RCM2()` fits **one data set**. With several stocks, it fits them together as one population, called a complex,
to that data set. The catches and indices in the data are summed over the stocks.
Use it for stocks that are fished and surveyed together, e.g., the sexes of one population. Stocks with separate data
need separate `RCM2()` calls.

| Stocks | Recruitment in the returned `om` |
|---|---|
| One stock | the fitted R0 |
| Several stocks, no `Herm` | every stock recruits; the fitted R0 is split by the input `SRR@R0` |
| Stocks linked by `Herm` | the stock that individuals start in gets the fitted R0; the `To` stocks get `R0 = 0` |

For several stocks:

- The fit uses natural mortality, weight and length-at-age averaged over the stocks, weighted by their unfished
  numbers-at-age.
- Every stock gets the fitted F and selectivity of each fleet, plus the fitted steepness and recruitment
  deviations.
- `fit@fits` has one fit, named by the complex (the stock names joined with `"-"`). `fit@OM@Complexes` has all
  the stocks in that complex.
- The stocks share the historical years in `data@Years` and their age classes.
- RCM is a single-area model, so an `om` with more than one area simulates a history close to, but not identical to,
  the fit. The examples use one area.

## Example data

The examples use MSEtool's `HermOM` (a protogynous grouper), with data from one simulated history. Catches and the
survey are summed over both sexes.

```{r data}
# One data object, summed over the stocks
sim_data <- function(om) {
  hist <- Simulate(om, silent = TRUE)
  yrs <- Years(om, "Historical")
  r <- Removals(hist); r <- r[r$Sim == 1 & r$Period == "Historical", ]
  b <- Biomass(hist);  b <- b[b$Sim == 1 & b$Period == "Historical", ]
  C <- tapply(r$Value, list(r$Year, r$Fleet), sum)
  B <- tapply(b$Value, b$Year, sum)
  dat <- Data(Years = yrs)
  dat@Landings <- CatchData(Name = colnames(C), Value = unname(C), CV = matrix(0.05, length(yrs), ncol(C)))
  dat@Survey <- IndicesData(Name = "Survey", Value = matrix(B, ncol = 1), CV = matrix(0.2, length(yrs), 1))
  dat
}

hm <- HermOM
hm@nSim <- 3
for (s in 1:2) hm@Stock[[s]]@Spatial <- Spatial()
dat <- sim_data(hm)
fleets <- hm@Fleet[[1]]
names(fleets)
```

## 1. One stock

```{r single}
fit1 <- RCM2(hm@Stock[[1]], data = dat, Fleet = fleets, nSim = 3, pYear = 10,
             s_selectivity = "B", silent = TRUE)
fit1
```

## 2. Several stocks without `Herm`

Here the two sexes have different growth but no sex change, and each recruits half the population. Pass a named
list of stocks and one data object. The list names become the stock names.

```{r several}
female <- hm@Stock[[1]]
male <- hm@Stock[[2]]
male@SRR <- female@SRR      # the HermOM male has no stock-recruit relationship of its own
female@SRR@SPFrom <- male@SRR@SPFrom <- NULL
female@SRR@R0 <- male@SRR@R0 <- 5000    # the shares of the fitted R0

fit2 <- RCM2(list(Female = female, Male = male), data = dat, Fleet = fleets,
             nSim = 3, pYear = 10, s_selectivity = "B", silent = TRUE)
fit2
names(fit2@fits)
fit2@OM@Stock$Female@SRR@R0 / (fit2@OM@Stock$Female@SRR@R0 + fit2@OM@Stock$Male@SRR@R0)
```

The input `SRR@R0` values only set the shares. If no stock has `SRR@R0`, the shares are equal.

Both stocks have an empty `SRR@SPFrom`, so each recruits from its own spawning output, with the fitted steepness.
The fit uses their summed spawning output. So the `om` history matches the fit exactly when the stocks have the same
biology, and is close when their biology differs. Recruiting stocks can instead share a source, e.g., both with the
same `SRR@SPFrom`. They then recruit from the same spawning output.

## 3. Hermaphroditic stocks

Link the stocks with a `stocktransition` object (`MSEtool::Herm()`). `Herm` only moves fish between the stocks.
As in MSEtool, two settings determine recruitment:

- **Where recruits go:** to the stock that individuals start in, i.e., the stock that is not the `To` stock of any
  transition. `RCM2()` sets `SRR@R0 = 0` for the other stocks.
- **Whose spawning output drives recruitment:** `SRR@SPFrom` of the recruiting stock, with an empty `SRR@SPFrom`
  meaning the stock itself. `RCM2()` keeps any `SRR@SPFrom` you set.

### Protogynous (females first)

The female stock recruits and spawns, so its empty `SPFrom` is right. The `HermOM` male has
`SRR@SPFrom = "Example Grouper Female Stock"`, the name of the female stock.

```{r herm}
female <- hm@Stock[[1]]
male <- hm@Stock[[2]]
female@SRR@SPFrom
male@SRR@SPFrom
frac <- hm@Herm[[1]]@Frac

fit3 <- RCM2(list(Female = female, Male = male), data = dat, Fleet = fleets,
             Herm = Herm(From = "Female", To = "Male", Frac = frac),
             nSim = 3, pYear = 10, s_selectivity = "B", silent = TRUE)
fit3
fit3@OM@Stock$Male@SRR@SPFrom
range(fit3@OM@Stock$Male@SRR@R0)
```

The list names replace `Stock@Name`. `RCM2()` renames the old stock names in `SRR@SPFrom`, and in `Herm@From` and
`Herm@To`, to the list names. Here `"Example Grouper Female Stock"` becomes `"Female"`.

The simulated female spawning biomass matches the fit:

```{r herm-check}
ssb_check <- function(fit, stock) {
  hist <- Simulate(fit@OM, silent = TRUE)
  sb <- SBiomass(hist)
  sb <- sb[sb$Period == "Historical" & sb$Stock == stock, ]
  sb <- tapply(sb$Value, list(sb$Sim, sb$Year), sum)
  max(abs(sb / fit@fits[[1]]@SSB[seq_len(nrow(sb)), seq_len(ncol(sb))] - 1))
}
ssb_check(fit3, "Female")
```

### Protandrous (males first)

The male stock recruits, so set its `SRR@SPFrom` to the female stock for recruitment to come from female spawning
output. Otherwise the males would recruit from their own spawning output, as in MSEtool. `SRR@SPFrom` can be the
stock name or its position in the list, here `1`. This example reuses the protogynous data to show the setup.

```{r protandry}
male_p <- male
male_p@SRR <- female@SRR   # the HermOM male has no stock-recruit relationship of its own
male_p@SRR@SPFrom <- 1     # Female, first in the list

fit4 <- RCM2(list(Female = female, Male = male_p), data = dat, Fleet = fleets,
             Herm = Herm(From = "Male", To = "Female", Frac = frac),
             nSim = 3, pYear = 10, s_selectivity = "B", silent = TRUE)
fit4@OM@Stock$Male@SRR@SPFrom
range(fit4@OM@Stock$Female@SRR@R0)
ssb_check(fit4, "Female")
```

### How `SRR@SPFrom` is read

`RCM2()` maps `SRR@SPFrom` to stock names as MSEtool does. It can be:

- A stock name, e.g., `"Female"`.
- A position in `Stock` (or in `OM@Stock`), e.g., `1`.
- A weight vector named by stock name or position, e.g., `c(Female = 0.7, Male = 0.3)` or `c("1" = 0.7, "2" = 0.3)`.
  Recruitment depends on spawning output relative to unfished, so the weights set the relative contribution of each
  source.

An empty `SRR@SPFrom` on a stock that does not recruit is set to the recruiting stock it comes from, unless that stock
is itself a spawning source.

## 4. An existing om

`RCM2(om)` conditions an `om` with one data object in `OM@Data`. Every stock is put in one complex. The other `om`
settings (name, `maxF`, `Obs`, `Imp`, ...) are kept.

```{r om}
hm@Data <- list(Grouper = dat)
RCM2(hm, s_selectivity = "B", silent = TRUE)
```

## Errors

- More than one data object (`data = list(d1, d2)`, or `OM@Data` of length > 1).
- `OM@Complexes` with more than one complex, or a complex without every stock.
- `SRR@SPFrom` that names a stock that is not in `Stock`.
- Several recruiting stocks whose `SRR@SPFrom` name different spawning sources (other than each its own), or with different `SRR@Model`.
- Seasonal models (`OM@Seasons > 1`).
- `drop_nonconv = TRUE` or `drop_highF = TRUE`, which drop simulations. Every simulation is kept in the `om`.
